en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on Exhortation 23.
The Training Rule Concerning the Nuns’ Quarters.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodha Monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus, having approached the nuns' quarters, were instructing the group-of-six bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunīs said this to the group-of-six bhikkhunīs:
"Come, noble ladies, let us go for the instruction."
“Venerable lady, even if we were to go for the sake of exhortation, the Venerable ones of the group-of-six would come right here and exhort us.
The bhikkhunīs complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying,
“How can the bhikkhus of the group-of-six go to the bhikkhunīs’ quarters and exhort the bhikkhunīs?”
Then those bhikkhunīs informed the bhikkhus of this matter.
Those bhikkhus who were few in desires... [as before]... were indignant, disparaged [the practice], and complained, saying:
"How can the group-of-six bhikkhus, having approached the bhikkhunīs' quarters, exhort the bhikkhunīs?"... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that you have gone to the nuns’ quarters and exhorted the bhikkhunīs?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you approach the dwelling place of the bhikkhunīs and exhort the bhikkhunīs?
This, foolish men, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“Whosoever bhikkhu, having approached the dwelling place of bhikkhunīs, should exhort the bhikkhunīs, commits a pācittiya offense.
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.
Now at that time, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī was ill.
The elder bhikkhus approached Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī; having approached, they said this to her:
“We hope, Gotamī, that you are bearing up; we hope that you are getting by?”
“Venerable ladies, I am not getting well; I cannot maintain myself.
“Come now, Venerable lady, please teach us the Dhamma.
“Sister, it is not permissible to approach the dwelling place of the bhikkhunīs and teach the Dhamma to the bhikkhunīs,” they thought, and being afraid of wrongdoing, they did not teach.
Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, approached Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī; having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī:
“I hope you are bearing up, Gotamī; I hope you are getting by?”
“Venerable sir, formerly elder bhikkhus would come and teach me the Dhamma,
and because of that I was at ease. But now, thinking,
‘It has been forbidden by the Blessed One,’ they do not teach out of fear of wrongdoing.”
“Because of that, I am not at ease.
Then the Blessed One, having instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī with a discourse on the Dhamma, rose from his seat and departed.
Then, on this occasion and in this context, the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, monks, having approached the nuns’ quarters, to exhort a sick nun.
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule:
‘Whatever monk, having approached the nuns’ quarters, should exhort the nuns, except on an appropriate occasion, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).’”
In this regard, this is the occasion: when a bhikkhunī is ill—this is the occasion therein.
“Whoever,” however, means whoever of such a kind... [and so on].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Bhikkhunī-upassaya" (a dwelling for bhikkhunīs) means:
"Where nuns stay even for a single night.
"Having approached" means having gone there.
"A bhikkhunī" means one who is fully ordained in both Saṅghas.
"Should exhort" means:
If she instructs [a nun] by means of the eight *garudhammas*, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
"Except at the proper time" means excluding the proper time.
"Ill" means that a nun is unable to go for the exhortation or to live in community.
If one who is fully ordained perceives another as fully ordained and, approaching the nuns' quarters, exhorts her except on the proper occasion, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
If one approaches a nunnery and, being in doubt as to whether she is fully ordained, gives her exhortation at a time other than the [permitted] occasion, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

If one approaches a nunnery and, perceiving her to be not fully ordained when she is actually fully ordained, gives her exhortation at a time other than the [permitted] occasion, there is an offense of expiation.
If one exhorts her by means of another teaching, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If he instructs one who is fully ordained on only one side [of the community], there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she is not fully ordained but he perceives her as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is not fully ordained but he is uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one perceives as not fully ordained a person who is not fully ordained, there is no offense.
There is no offense at the proper time.
When giving a summary,
when giving a detailed questioning,
or when being told, "Venerable one, please recite," he recites.
She asks a question;
when asked a question, she speaks;
and while he is speaking for the sake of another, the bhikkhunīs listen.
For a trainee nun,
for a novice nun,
for one who is insane,
"For the first offender":
the third training rule concerning the nuns' quarters is concluded.
